brief: Yesterday's AI/semis selloff (Semis -7%, AI-levered -6%, AI data centers -8%) drove GS's HF Popular Pair Basket (GSTHVIPP) down 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, and pushed Global Fundamental L/S, multi-strat and systematic strategies all down more than 1% on the same day for the first time since Covid. Futures show tentative, not fully convincing stabilization this morning, with crude up 1.5% (WTI above $100) and the 10-year yield at 4.98%. Overnight AI-adjacent earnings (WDC, BE, FIX, MXL) mostly beat but produced mixed-to-lower stock reactions; GS expects WDC to trade lower despite strong results because competitor (believed Toshiba) capacity additions could cap HDD multiples, and prefers Seagate on relative pricing momentum. SpaceX is in talks to access 80,000 cell sites, lifting tower stocks (AMT/SBAC/CCI) and pressuring carriers (T/TMUS/VZ), including lease talks with Crown Castle toward building a fourth nationwide carrier. Oracle's October 29 Investor Day arrives amid AI-infrastructure capacity debate; GS flags an inflection in OCI gross profit within 12 months as the key company-specific dynamic to watch.
